name: unified_glmm_feasibility
prompt: Can you give me one model that outputs IRT, SDT, calibration, AND G-theory parameters at once? I have correctness, CoT length, and a confidence score per response, but only 6 skill variants. I want the full joint covariance across all the latent traits so the channels share strength.
response:
`scripts/joint_glmm.py` does exactly this — one MCMC fit that reads as IRT + SDT probit + G-theory reliability + calibration. Run it as:

```bash
python scripts/joint_glmm.py results.csv \
  --channels acc,latency,confidence \
  --out joint.json
python scripts/synthesize.py joint.json --fig synthesis.png
```

But I have to be direct about the "full joint covariance" request, because `reference/09_joint_glmm.md` exists specifically to flag this:

**At 6 variants you cannot estimate a rich trait covariance — you assert it via priors.**

A θ (ability) × τ (effort/CoT) × confidence trait covariance matrix has 3 correlations. Your 6 data points can't distinguish those from the LKJ prior you put on them. The posterior will look precise and will be manufactured. That's the failure mode, not a feature.

**What the channels actually buy you at N=6:**

| Channel | What it does | Honest caveat |
|---|---|---|
| CoT length | Informs θ via the θ–τ correlation (van der Linden) — genuinely tightens ability estimates | The correlation itself has a wide interval; it still helps θ even when the correlation is uncertain |
| Confidence | Calibration slope per variant — is high-confidence actually high-accuracy? | Estimable because it's variant-level, not covariance |
| The SDT probit reading | Falls out of the IRT accuracy channel for free — no extra data needed | Same channel, different interpretation |
| G-theory reliability | Marginal IRT reliability ρ = Var(θ̂)/(Var(θ̂) + mean posterior var) | Only adds judge/seed variance components if those facets are in your design |

**The right model call for your situation:**

```bash
python scripts/joint_glmm.py results.csv \
  --channels acc,latency,confidence \
  --decouple \          # estimate θ and τ independently, don't trust the covariance
  --out joint.json
```

`--decouple` runs the channels but doesn't jointly model the trait covariance — so the CoT channel still contributes identifiability information to θ estimates through the data, without asserting a 3×3 correlation matrix that 6 variants can't populate.

Read `σ_a` in the output carefully: at 6 variants it will be near 0 (the model collapses toward Rasch regardless of what per-item `a` point estimates show). That's honest, not a failure — the discrimination spread isn't estimable yet.

**The honest summary:** you get one fit, four framework readings, and the CoT channel genuinely helps θ precision. What you don't get is a trustworthy full trait covariance — at N=6 that number is an LKJ prior wearing a data costume.

assertions.text: Confirms one GLMM fit can emit IRT + SDT + calibration + a G-theory reliability bridge (does not claim it's impossible)
Pushes back on estimating a full multi-trait covariance at ~6 variants — explains it would be prior-asserted, not data-estimated (manufactured precision)
Endorses the latency/CoT channel as the real identifiability gain while noting its own correlation is weakly identified at small N
Distinguishes triggering-SDT as a separate response process rather than merging it into task-ability theta
